clue.text: Holy man runs incense for foreigner

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to incense someone is to anger them, the verb sense

explanation.surface: A priest burns incense and is mistaken for someone from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' reads as the perfumed smoke a holy man burns, but here it is the verb meaning to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outsider not known locally, someone from elsewhere.

clue.text: Entice tailless water fowl within grasp

indicators.note: within means the shortened bird goes inside the word for grasp

parts.note: to grasp is to see, as in understand

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut from the bird

parts.note: a duck is a water fowl

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail is lured within reach of a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' leaves DUC, and 'within' places it; grasp here means understand, not hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lead astray by tempting or luring.

clue.text: Criticises cooks

definitions.meaning: criticises in the sense of savagely pans or slates
cooks in an oven with dry heat

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: harshly criticises someone, and cooks meat by baking in an oven.

clue.text: Tend to race back to Home Counties

indicators.note: back means the word for race is written in reverse

parts.note: to run is to race
the Home Counties around London are in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Someone tends to rush back to the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tend to' reads as 'be inclined to' but is the verb phrase for caring for someone. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to care for the sick or injured, look after.

clue.text: Ban English doctor on Greek ship

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree, so a doctor
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: An English doctor is barred from boarding a Greek vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official prohibition, especially on trade.

clue.text: Considers dropping thousand for good stuff

indicators.note: dropping one letter for another means the thousand letter is swapped out and replaced by the good letter

parts.note: to consider is to think, so considers gives thinks

explanation.surface: Someone weighs whether to give up a large sum in exchange for something better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping thousand for good' swaps the K of THINKS for a G.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belongings or odds and ends are loosely called stuff.

clue.text: Horse's trail bends around ramshackle farm

indicators.note: around means the bends go round the outside of the jumbled letters

parts.note: hooks are bends or curves

indicators.note: ramshackle means tumbledown, so the letters of farm are disordered

explanation.surface: A horse's tracks wind around a tumbledown farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramshackle' gives FMAR, which 'around' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the prints left in the ground by hooves form a horse's trail.

clue.text: Symbols used to represent people binding books

indicators.note: binding means wrapping round, so the people word encloses the books

parts.note: a nation is a people
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Symbols stand for people who bind books.
explanation.walkthrough: OT, the Old Testament, is a standard crossword shorthand for books.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a system of written signs, as in musical or mathematical notation.

clue.text: Generous fairytale creature the French found aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means placed inside the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship
an elf is a creature of fairytales
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted elf and some French people are discovered stowed on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: putting others first, unstintingly giving.

clue.text: Admiral regularly getting family abuse

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word admiral, starting from the second

parts.note: a tribe is a large family or clan

explanation.surface: A naval officer is regularly bad-mouthed by his own relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of Admiral: D, I, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a torrent of abusive criticism.

clue.text: Entrance men starting to travel in China

indicators.note: in means the soldiers and the opening letter are placed inside the word for a friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers or men

indicators.note: starting to means only the first letter of travel is used

explanation.surface: A group of men set off to tour China and find their way in.
explanation.walkthrough: China is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a doorway or gateway, especially an imposing one.

clue.text: Bullet belt

definitions.meaning: a piece of ammunition fired from a gun
belt as a verb, to hit hard

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a lump of metal fired from a gun, and to strike someone hard with a punch.

clue.text: Each dart shot bit of light into place of worship

indicators.note: shot here means broken or ruined, so the letters of each dart are mixed up
a bit of the word light is its first letter

explanation.surface: A darts player flings each dart at a beam of light inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges EACH DART into CATHEDRA, then 'bit of light' adds L.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the principal church of a diocese, seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Element found in motorway and elsewhere

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
et al. is Latin et alibi, and elsewhere

explanation.surface: Something turns up on the motorway and in other places too.
explanation.walkthrough: et al. is usually 'and others' (et alii) but can also stand for et alibi, 'and elsewhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: iron, copper and gold are chemical elements of this class.

clue.text: Made money holding rally

indicators.note: holding means the phrase made money contains the letters, which sit across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone earned cash by staging a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a protest march or public demonstration of support.

clue.text: Cosmetic agreement had misery rising all around

indicators.note: all around means the misery word surrounds the agreement and had
rising in a down clue means the misery word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: woe is misery
yes is a word of agreement
taken as written

explanation.surface: Make-up that was agreed on brought gloom all round.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' gives EOW, and 'all around' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: coloured powder applied to the eyelids is a cosmetic.

clue.text: Monsters and thugs boxing outside of ring

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the thugs hold the other letters inside them

parts.note: goons are hired thugs

indicators.note: the outside of ring is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Monsters and hoodlums are fighting just beyond the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' and 'ring' suggest a prize fight, but 'boxing' only means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Medusa and her sisters, the snake-haired monsters of Greek myth.

clue.text: Great and favourable point discovered

parts.note: a pro is a point in favour, as in pros and cons
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A great and helpful point has been uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: of great depth or intensity, as in profound relief.

clue.text: Worships one cheat going to foreign isles

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to do someone is to cheat them

indicators.note: foreign suggests strange or altered, so the letters of isles are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worshipper and a swindler head off to some exotic islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges ISLES into LISES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: adores or reveres excessively, as one might a god.

clue.text: Socialist leader such as Kinnock perhaps?

parts.note: red is the traditional colour and nickname of socialists
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A left-wing party leader such as Neil Kinnock, the former Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Kinnock, Labour leader in the 1980s, was a socialist leader and famously ginger-haired, so the whole clue also works as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Kinnock is well known for his ginger hair, the 'perhaps' marking him as one instance.

clue.text: Throw from university fellow taking wicket

indicators.note: taking means the fellow holds the wicket letter inside

parts.note: a don is a university teacher or fellow
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket ball is thrown by an academic who takes a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to knock or bring someone to the ground, as a wrestler does.

clue.text: Corrupt foundation

definitions.meaning: corrupt in the sense of low, immoral or debased
the bottom or support something rests on

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: morally low or ignoble, and the bottom supporting layer of a structure.

clue.text: Has-been cast as female spirit

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faded actor is cast in the role of a ghostly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like casting a part in a play, but signals the rearrangement of HAS-BEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Irish folklore a wailing woman spirit whose cry foretells death.

clue.text: Team left Europe in uniform

indicators.note: in means left and Europe are placed inside the word for uniform

parts.note: even means uniform or regular

explanation.surface: A side has left Europe dressed in its kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like a team strip, but here it means even.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: football and cricket sides each field this many players, hence a team.

clue.text: Like craft capsizing on lake belonging to star

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: capsizing means turning over, so in a down clue the craft word is read backwards

parts.note: art is craft or skill

explanation.surface: A boat overturns on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat, which is what 'capsizing' plays on, but it means skill, ART, turned to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: relating to the stars, stellar.

clue.text: Take something the wrong way?

parts.note: taking something the wrong way usually means being offended, but here it is taking an item dishonestly, that is stealing

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom suggests misunderstanding a remark; read literally it means taking an object by the wrong means, theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to steal something small or of little value, pilfer.

clue.text: Will keeps changing mind ahead of opening of sweet factories

indicators.note: ahead of puts the will-and-mind part before the last letter
keeps means the word will holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: changing tells us to rearrange the letters of mind
the opening of sweet is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone keeps changing their mind before starting on the sweet course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' gives INDM, which 'keeps' holds after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mill is a factory, and these were milling works driven by sails.

clue.text: Excellence encountered around Royal Institution

indicators.note: around means the word for encountered goes round the institution letters

parts.note: met means encountered
RI is the abbreviation for the Royal Institution, a British scientific body

explanation.surface: Distinction was found at a famous scientific society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Institution is a London science body.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: worth, quality deserving praise.

clue.text: Positive and proper Greek character with skin of doe

parts.note: U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable or proper
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the skin of doe is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A cheerful, well-bred Greek is described along with a deer's hide.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class, hence proper, usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the good or favourable aspect of a situation, its advantage.

clue.text: Admire husband and wife returning to some place or other

indicators.note: returning means the admire-husband-wife string is read backwards

parts.note: to revere is to admire deeply

explanation.surface: A married couple, much admired, go back home or somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses REVEREHW.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to whatever place, to any location at all.

clue.text: Reject half of meal featuring pig

indicators.note: featuring means containing, so the pig is placed within the half meal
half of means only the first three letters of the evening meal word

parts.note: dinner is a meal
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone turns down half a meal that has pork in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the first three letters of the six-letter evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to renounce or refuse to acknowledge as one's own.

clue.text: Head of security sacked lenient guard

indicators.note: the head of security is its first letter
sacked means wrecked or plundered, so the letters of lenient are scrambled

explanation.surface: The security chief fires a guard for being too soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges LENIENT into ENTINEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sentry or watchman posted to keep guard.
